add.title: Penitenciarias Nacionales de Honduras: una tortura para personas LGTBI - Corresponsales Clave
add.summary: Corresponsales Clave (trans activist Kendra Jordany, 6 Sep 2017), drawing on the torture-prevention centre CPTRT: trans women in Honduras' national penitentiaries are held in the MEN'S system. At Penitenciaria Nacional Tamara, LGBTI prisoners are concentrated in the 'La Isla' module (located beside the mentally-ill unit); trans women are forced to cut their hair and barred from presenting as women ('la policia... dicen que ellas son hombres'); conjugal visits are denied. At Penitenciaria de Marcala authorities seized a trans woman's clothes and cut her hair, and only after CPTRT intervention was she isolated from the men and her feminine belongings returned. Documents birth-sex placement with de facto LGBTI grouping and ad-hoc protective isolation, and no placement-by-gender-identity policy.

add.title: HRW, 'Every Day I Live in Fear': Violence and Discrimination Against LGBT People in El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, and Obstacles to Asylum in the United States
add.summary: Human Rights Watch (7 Oct 2020), Honduras section: 'Honduras places transgender women in men's prisons, which can lead to physical and sexual abuse.' A Honduran judge told HRW of a case in which a trans woman was raped by fellow detainees with the complicity of prison guards; the judge said she had informed prosecutors, who did not investigate: 'There's no way to protect trans women in men's prisons.' Independent confirmation that placement operates by birth sex in the men's system, with documented sexual violence and official inaction (as of 2020).
